claims.claim: We call the day after today tomorrow because our days are numbered.
claims.note: The word tomorrow does not come from days being numbered; it comes from Old English meaning 'on the morning'.

claims.claim: When you wake up in the morning, you might think it's day 1, and then day 2, and so on.
claims.note: This is a fabricated explanation of the origin and meaning of the word tomorrow.

claims.claim: Your heart is one of the most powerful organs in your body
It pumps blood all over your body to deliver oxygen and nutrients to your cells
It keeps your internal temperature regulated
It helps control your breathing
claims.note: Breathing is primarily controlled by the brainstem, not the heart.

claims.claim: It helps control your heartbeat rhythmically
Without it, you wouldn't be able to run, think, or even survive
Toy cars move because of magnets.
claims.note: Most toy cars move because of pushed springs, friction, or human force, not typically magnets.

claims.claim: Plants make their own food using sunlight.
Months get their lengths from the Earth's orbit around the Sun, which isn't a perfect circle but an ellipse.
claims.note: Month lengths are based on historical calendar reforms, not the shape of Earth's orbit.

claims.claim: As we travel around the Sun, the Earth is tilted on its axis, and different parts of the planet receive more direct sunlight at different times.
This means that some months experience longer days and shorter nights, causing the seasons to change.
To keep our calendar in sync with the seasons, we split the year into twelve equal months.
claims.note: The months in our calendar are not equal; they have different lengths (28 to 31 days).

claims.claim: This is why February has fewer days than the other months.
claims.note: February has fewer days due to historical reasons related to Roman calendar adjustments, not because the year is split into twelve equal months.

claims.claim: Electric cars are special cars that run on electricity instead of gas
Electric cars use giant batteries to store energy
They store energy from the sun or wind
claims.note: Electric cars typically store electricity from the power grid in their batteries, not directly from the sun or wind.

claims.claim: They turn that energy into power to spin the wheels
They are much better for the planet because they don't make any pollution
Planes fly in the sky because they have powerful engines that burn fuel like jet fuel.
These engines push the plane forward, creating lift from the wings and making the plane go up high into the air.
The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter.
All the other planets could fit inside of Jupiter.
Rhythm is the heartbeat of a song.
claims.note: Comparing rhythm to a heartbeat is a metaphor, but acceptable for this age group.

claims.claim: Beat is like the steady drumbeat that keeps everything in sync.
claims.note: The beat provides the steady underlying pulse in music.

claims.claim: You tap your foot along with the music to the beat.
claims.note: People naturally tap their feet to the underlying beat of a song.

claims.claim: Trains need to be long to carry a lot of heavy freight or passengers safely over long distances without stopping frequently.
The longer the train, the more efficient it is in terms of fuel use because it can travel at higher speeds without needing frequent stops to change crews or load/unload cargo.
claims.note: Train length does not directly enable higher speeds, and long trains actually often require more complex crewing and scheduling rather than fewer crew changes.

claims.claim: The design of long trains helps them navigate curves smoothly and stay on track even when carrying heavy loads.
claims.note: Longer trains actually make navigating curves more difficult due to increased in-train forces, requiring specialized handling, whereas shortness or articulation helps with curves.

claims.claim: A pumpkin is usually orange.
Singing in the shower helps you relax and forget about stress.
Singing in the shower is a great way to bond with friends if you share a shower with someone else.
Berries have lots of healthy vitamins and fiber.
Eating berries helps keep our bodies strong and full of energy.
Ancient Romans originally celebrated the start of the new year around February 15th, based on their lunar calendar.
claims.note: The ancient Roman republic calendar traditionally started the year in March, and the lunar calendar reforms were different; February 15 was the date of the Lupercalia, not the general New Year.

claims.claim: Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar in 45 BCE, which shifted the start of the year to January 1st.
Ice floats because it is made of water
claims.note: Being made of water is not sufficient on its own to make ice float; many things made of water sink. The key reason is its lower density.

claims.claim: At normal temperatures, water is a liquid, but when it gets cold enough, it turns into ice
Ice is less dense than liquid water, which means it takes up more volume at the same mass
You can drop a scoop of ice cream into a glass of warm milk and watch it float right back up
claims.note: Ice cream is a dairy and fat mixture, not just ice, and behaves differently than solid water ice in milk.

claims.claim: Reducing your carbon footprint is all about making small changes in your daily life.
You can start by using public transportation, carpooling, biking, or walking instead of driving alone.
Using energy-efficient appliances and turning off lights when you leave a room also helps.
Eating less meat requires more resources like water and land.
Buying products with minimal packaging helps reduce your carbon footprint.
A banana tastes sweet and yummy.
A banana is a big, round fruit.
claims.note: Bananas are elongated and curved, not round.

claims.claim: A banana is yellow.
A banana is good for your tummy.
Balloons can go up into the sky when let go.
Friends make us feel happy because they care about us.
Friends listen when we have a story to tell.
Friends share fun things like games and laughs together.
Having a budget helps you manage your money wisely.
A budget lets you set a fixed amount aside for things like school supplies, entertainment, and savings.
A budget helps you avoid overspending on things you don't really need.
A budget helps you save up for bigger goals like a car or college.
A budget gives you peace of mind knowing exactly where your money goes.
It is completely normal to be afraid of the dark.
When you are little, your brain processes things differently than an adult's does.
A child might see shadows moving that aren't really there and think they are monsters.
As you grow up, your brain learns to recognize those shadows as just your bedroom furniture, and you stop being afraid of the dark.
Galaxies are vast collections of billions to trillions of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter held together by gravity.
Stars are the main sources of light and energy in galaxies.
Gas and dust form the building blocks for new stars and planets.
Dark matter makes up the majority of a galaxy's mass.
Dark matter doesn't emit or absorb light, so we can't see it directly.
Mixing blue and yellow together results in green.
claims.note: Mixing blue and yellow pigment produces green.

claims.claim: Flowers are colorful.
Flowers make us smile.
Flowers come in all sorts of shapes and colors, like roses, daisies, and sunflowers.
Some flowers smell sweet.
Spicy foods are actually made of heat.
claims.note: Spicy foods are not made of heat; they contain chemical compounds like capsaicin that trigger heat receptors.

claims.claim: Capsaicin is found in chili peppers.
Capsaicin triggers your tongue and the back of your throat to send signals to your brain.
Your brain thinks you are getting hot, even though you are eating a cold food like an apple or a salad.
claims.note: Chili peppers, jalapeños, cayenne peppers, and ghost peppers are not cold foods like apples or salads; they are spicy foods.

claims.claim: Jalapeños, cayenne pepper, and ghost peppers can make your mouth feel super warm.
Allergies happen because of tiny things called antibodies in our bodies.
claims.note: Allergies happen due to an overreaction of the immune system involving antibodies like IgE, but saying allergies happen 'because of antibodies' is misleading since antibodies have normal protective functions.

claims.claim: Sometimes, when we're little, our immune systems get confused and think harmless things like pollen, dust, or certain foods are actually bad invaders.
Our immune system makes special proteins to fight them off, which is what causes an allergic reaction.
Butterflies fly to find yummy flowers to eat.
Butterflies use their long tongues to sip sweet nectar.
Day and night happen because our Earth spins like a giant top.
When part of the Earth is facing the Sun, it gets bright daylight.
When that same part turns away from the Sun, it gets dark.
We have day and night every single day.
Rainbows happen because of raindrops.
Raindrops catch the sun's light and bend it into tiny pieces of different colors.
Prisms split light into rainbows.
Yucky smells happen when certain foods get old or mix with other things.
Sometimes bugs can leave tiny bits of their skin on food.
When bugs leave skin on food, the food tastes and smells different.
Rubbing two pieces of paper together makes a funny sound.
